messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Take gabapentin exactly as prescribed. Your dose may differ from the ranges shown here.
Usual Gabapentin Dose for Epilepsy (immediate-release):
Patients 12 years and older Dose: starting dose gabapentin 300 mg 3 times a day, which may be titrated up to a maximum dose of 600 mg 3 times a day if needed.
Patients 3 to 11 years of age Dose: the starting dose range is 10 to 15 mg/kg/day, given in 3 divided doses. The recommended dose in patients 3 to 4 years of age is 40 mg/kg/day, and in patients 5 to 11 years of age is 25 to 35 mg/kg/day, given in 3 divided doses. The recommended maintenance dose is reached by upward titration over approximately 3 days.
Less than 3 years: Not recommended
Note:
- Leave no more than 12 hours between doses
- Dose should be adjusted in patients with reduced kidney function. Your doctor will determine your dose based on your kidney function.
Use: Adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial onset seizures, with and without secondary generalization, in patients 3 years of age and older.
Usual Adult Dose for Postherpetic Neuralgia (immediate-release):
Triples: [["Gabapentin", "has administration instruction", "take exactly as prescribed"], ["Gabapentin", "has recommended dose", "300 mg three times a day for patients 12 years and older"], ["Gabapentin", "has maximum recommended dose", "600 mg three times a day for patients 12 years and older"], ["Gabapentin", "has recommended dose", "10 to 15 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses for patients 3 to 11 years of age"], ["Gabapentin", "has recommended dose", "40 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses for patients 3 to 4 years of age"], ["Gabapentin", "has recommended dose", "25 to 35 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses for patients 5 to 11 years of age"], ["Gabapentin", "has maintenance dose instruction", "reached by upward titration over approximately 3 days"], ["Gabapentin", "not recommended for", "patients less than 3 years of age"], ["Gabapentin", "has dosing interval instruction", "leave no more than 12 hours between doses"], ["Gabapentin", "has dose adjustment instruction", "adjust in patients with reduced kidney function"], ["Gabapentin", "treats", "partial onset seizures with secondary generalization"], ["Gabapentin", "treats", "partial onset seizures without secondary generalization"], ["Gabapentin", "has indication", "adjunctive therapy in patients 3 years of age and older"], ["Gabapentin", "has indication", "postherpetic neuralgia in adults"]]
Relations: ["has administration instruction", "has dose adjustment instruction", "has dosing interval instruction", "has indication", "has maintenance dose instruction", "has maximum recommended dose", "has recommended dose", "not recommended for", "treats"]
Answer:

completion:
has administration instruction: The subject drug should be taken according to the specific instructions specified by the object entity.  
has dose adjustment instruction: The subject drug's dose should be modified in patients with the specified medical condition.  
has dosing interval instruction: The subject drug should be administered with no more than the specified time interval between doses.  
has indication: The subject drug is indicated for use in treating the specified medical condition.  
has maintenance dose instruction: The recommended maintenance dose of the subject drug is achieved through a gradual increase over the specified period.  
has maximum recommended dose: The highest dose of the subject drug recommended for the specified patient group is specified by the object entity.  
has recommended dose: The subject drug is recommended to be administered at the dose level specified by the object entity for the given patient group.  
not recommended for: The subject drug is not advised for use in patients with the specified condition.  
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
